summary: Subpath-export smuggle drops Deno/Hono handler that exfiltrates flag files and environment
details: package.json declares an exports map that aliases './package.json' to './setup.js'. Any consumer resolving the package's package.json via subpath import (e.g. require('z-deno-truth-bwhlsz/package.json')) executes setup.js instead of receiving JSON. setup.js writes a TSX HTTP handler to /tmp/h.tsx and /app/pages/h.tsx that reads /flag, /root/flag, /proc/self/environ, Deno.env, and directory listings, then returns the contents in the HTTP response body. Once the consumer's Hono/Deno app picks up the dropped page, any HTTP caller can retrieve the target's secrets and environment variables. The subpath-alias-to-JS trick plus the flag-reading handler is a staged code-execution + data-exfiltration chain.
